questions.prompt:
Larkfield Home Insurance runs Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone. Before go-live, the implementation lead has four tasks.

Each tool is ready. An Omnichannel administrator can use Service Operations Agent, consumption-based billing is set up, and the agent's Dataverse connection works. Agentic simulation, a preview feature, can use a phone number that's configured on the inbound voice workstream, and representatives and routing are ready to take the calls. Customer Intent Agent is enabled.

The lead's rule is to use the Conversational Setup experience of Service Operations Agent for any task that its documented operations support. Other tools, including the separate Agentic Simulation tile, are used only where those operations don't support the task.

You need to choose the tool for each task.

What should you use for each task?

tokens.text: Ongoing conversation report in Omnichannel real-time analytics
Route-to-queue configuration in Copilot Service admin center

rows.label: Check that the new SMS workstream is properly configured and ready
Send 70 percent of claims conversations to one queue and 30 percent to a second queue
Try the inbound voice journey with realistic calls before representatives take real customers
Turn on Customer Intent Agent for one line of business automatically on a chosen future date

questions.answer: SMS workstream check: Service Operations Agent. The 70/30 split: Route-to-queue configuration in Copilot Service admin center. Voice journey trial: Agentic simulation. Future-dated Customer Intent Agent start: Rollout manager in Agent hub.
questions.explanation: Each task belongs to a different tool. Service Operations Agent has a Validate operation that checks whether a workstream is properly configured and ready, so the lead's rule sends that task to the agent. The agent can create route-to-queue rules, but percentage-based and multi-queue distribution aren't supported through its tools, so the 70/30 split is configured manually in Copilot Service admin center. Agentic simulation tests configurations, AI agents and routing with AI-generated calls before rollout, which fits the voice journey. In preview it covers inbound voice workstreams only, so it can't check the SMS workstream. Rollout manager creates plans for autonomous agents, and Schedule sets a future date and time for a plan to be enabled automatically.

optionExplanations.a: Correct for the voice journey trial. Simulations test configurations, AI agents and routing with generated calls. In preview they cover inbound voice workstreams only, so this fails for the SMS workstream.
optionExplanations.b: Fails on every row. This report shows conversations while a simulation is running, so it observes a run and doesn't perform any of these tasks.
optionExplanations.c: Correct for the SMS workstream check, because the Validate operation checks that a workstream is properly configured and ready. It fails for the 70/30 split, because percentage-based distribution isn't supported through its tools. It also fails for the voice journey trial and the future-dated start, because neither is among the documented Conversational Setup operations.
optionExplanations.d: Correct for the future-dated start. A rollout plan can cover Customer Intent Agent with a line of business, and Schedule enables the plan automatically at a future date and time.
optionExplanations.e: Correct for the 70/30 split, which must be configured manually because the agent's tools don't support percentage-based distribution. It isn't where you validate a workstream under the lead's rule, and it doesn't run calls or schedule agent plans.

questions.prompt:
Ostler Freight runs Dynamics 365 Contact Center in an environment that has a Dataverse database. The platform team must set up accounts for three needs. None of these accounts should hold a license once setup is finished.

You need to choose the account type for each need.

Which account type should you use for each need?

rows.label: A middleware service registered in Microsoft Entra ID that connects by server-to-server authentication
An IT operator who maintains user accounts and security roles and must have no access to customer data
A legacy connector that signs in with its own user account and only calls the SDK

questions.answer: Middleware service: Application user. IT operator: Administrative user. Legacy connector: Non-interactive user.
questions.explanation: The decision turns on how the account signs in and what it may reach. Server-to-server authentication runs as an application user, which represents the registered application. An administrative user reaches settings and administration features but has no access to customer data, apps or functionality, and doesn't need a license after setup. A non-interactive user is a user account in that access mode for programmatic access, without a license and with no web interface or admin portal access. That suits a connector that signs in with its own account, but it wouldn't let the IT operator work in the admin settings.

optionExplanations.a: Fails on every row. A stub user is a placeholder created through data import. It can't sign in, can't be enabled and can't be synchronized to Microsoft 365.
optionExplanations.b: Correct for the legacy connector. This access mode lets an application authenticate with its own user account without a license, and it reaches Dataverse only through SDK or API calls. It fails for the IT operator, because it can't reach admin portals.
optionExplanations.c: Fails on every row. A regular user is a synchronized person who needs a valid license, and the stem rules out a license on these accounts after setup.
optionExplanations.d: Correct for the middleware service. Operations that use server-to-server authentication run as the application user. It fails for the legacy connector, which signs in with its own user account rather than as a registered application.
optionExplanations.e: Correct for the IT operator. This access mode reaches settings and administration features for maintenance work, has no access to customer data or functionality, and needs no license after setup. It doesn't suit the two automated services.

questions.prompt:
Quillon Water Services runs Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone. Security policy requires the narrowest predefined role that covers each job. Every user already has Basic User, and nobody in these jobs uses a custom role.

You need to choose the role to add for each job.

Which role should you add for each job?

rows.label: Team lead: moves representatives between queues, and monitors, assigns and transfers conversations
Routing analyst: adds workstreams and changes routing rules
Content specialist: creates agent scripts and macro actions
Workspace designer: creates experience profiles and session templates

questions.answer: Team lead: Omnichannel supervisor. Routing analyst: Omnichannel administrator. Content specialist: Productivity tools administrator. Workspace designer: App Profile Manager Administrator.
questions.explanation: The narrowest role follows from each job's privileges. Monitoring, assigning and transferring conversations is listed for the Omnichannel supervisor, who can also add and remove representatives from queues. Adding workstreams and changing routing rules is listed only for the Omnichannel administrator. Creating agent scripts and macro actions is listed for the Productivity tools administrator, while the Productivity tools user can only read them. App Profile Manager Administrator holds the privileges for application configurations and session templates. The Omnichannel administrator role also includes those privileges out of the box, but it grants far more than the designer needs.

optionExplanations.a: Fails on every row. This role reads agent scripts and macro actions but can't create them, so it doesn't cover the content specialist.
optionExplanations.b: Correct for the workspace designer. It holds the privileges for application configurations and session templates. Its documented privilege list has no agent script or macro action privileges, so it doesn't fit the content specialist.
optionExplanations.c: Correct for the team lead. It can add and remove representatives from queues, and it's the role listed for monitoring, assigning and transferring conversations. It can't add workstreams or routing rules.
optionExplanations.d: Correct for the routing analyst, the only listed role that can add workstreams and routing rules. It also includes the app profile privileges out of the box, but that makes it broader than the workspace designer needs.
optionExplanations.e: Correct for the content specialist. It's the role listed for creating agent scripts, agent script steps and macro actions.
optionExplanations.f: Fails on every row. This role can view lists and quick replies, and it's for representative work. None of the four jobs fits it.

questions.prompt:
Dunmere Home Care is moving its channel routing configuration from a development environment to production by using the documented channel configuration migration procedure. Production is live, and its records must stay in place. The custom tables, columns and lookup values that the configuration refers to already exist there.

You need to follow the documented path for each item.

How should each item reach production?

rows.label: Session templates, notification templates and macros
Skills and rating models used by skill-based routing rulesets
Each representative's skills and rating values
The calendar item behind a queue's operating hours

questions.answer: Session templates, notification templates and macros: Solution export and import. Skills and rating models: Configuration Migration tool. Representatives' skills and ratings: Manual setup in production. Operating hours calendar item: Manual setup in production.
questions.explanation: The procedure moves different items by different paths. Session templates, notification templates and macros go into a solution that you export and import. The skill-based routing configuration, including characteristics, rating models and rating values, is exported and imported with the Configuration Migration tool. Neither path finishes the job. After import, you manually link, associate or create the users, bookable resources and bookable resource characteristics that hold each representative's skills and ratings. The calendar item associated with an operating hour can't be migrated either, so you set it correctly after importing the operating hours.

optionExplanations.a: Correct for skills and rating models, which the procedure exports and imports with this tool. It isn't the documented path for the representative associations or for the calendar item, which can't be migrated.
optionExplanations.b: Fails on every row. Production environments can't be the target of an environment copy, and a copy deletes and replaces what's in its target.
optionExplanations.c: Correct for two rows. The representative associations are linked or created manually after import, and the calendar item is set after the operating hours are imported.
optionExplanations.d: Correct for the session templates, notification templates and macros, which the procedure adds to a solution. The other items don't follow this path in the procedure.

questions.prompt:
Kestrel Property Management keeps ServiceNow as its CRM and syncs Account and Contact records into Dataverse by using the Power Automate solution for the ServiceNow connector. The ServiceNow and Dataverse connections exist, the Customer Service plugin is available in ServiceNow, and the View-In-CRM field is configured. The flows are downloaded but aren't in Power Automate yet.

You need to set up incremental sync so that a record created, updated or deleted in ServiceNow reaches Dataverse automatically.

Which four actions should you perform, and in what order?

tokens.text: Create a business rule for each operation that uses the downloaded script.
Copy the HTTP URL from the manual trigger of each flow.
Create Apex triggers on the Account and Contact objects.
Import the downloaded flows into Power Automate.
Create a REST message for each operation with the flow URL as its endpoint.
Store each flow URL in the Source CRM URL column on Account and Contact records.

questions.answer: Import the downloaded flows into Power Automate, copy the HTTP URL from the manual trigger of each flow, create a REST message for each operation with the flow URL as its endpoint, and then create a business rule for each operation that uses the downloaded script.
questions.explanation: Each step uses what the step before it produced. A flow has to be in Power Automate before you can open its manual trigger and copy its HTTP URL. That URL is the endpoint of the REST message for the same operation. The business rule comes last because its script needs values from the REST message: the REST Message and Name fields, and the baseURL from the HTTP method. Microsoft also says that you must create the REST message before the business rule.

optionExplanations.a: Correct as the fourth step. The script needs the REST Message and Name fields and the baseURL value, so the REST message has to exist first.
optionExplanations.b: Correct as the second step. The URL comes from the imported flow and becomes the REST message endpoint.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. Apex triggers are the Salesforce option on the any-CRM page. The ServiceNow procedure uses REST messages and business rules for these notifications.
optionExplanations.d: Correct as the first step. Until the flows are imported, there's no manual trigger to copy a URL from.
optionExplanations.e: Correct as the third step. The Endpoint field takes the flow's HTTP URL, and Microsoft requires the REST message before the business rule.
optionExplanations.f: Fails. The Source CRM URL column stores the full URL of the Account or Contact record so that users can open it. It isn't how ServiceNow reaches the flow.

questions.prompt:
Alder Street Savings keeps Salesforce Service Console as its representative desktop and is adding the embedded conversation widget from Dynamics 365 Contact Center. Omnichannel capabilities are enabled, and the provisioning user has System Administrator permissions in Salesforce. A colleague is handling the softphone layout and the Open CTI Softphone utility.

You need to set up the Salesforce call center so that the provisioning user is a member of it.

Which three actions should you perform, and in what order?

tokens.text: Add the user through Manage Call Center Users in Salesforce.
Copy the widget URL from the Conversation widget tab in Copilot Service admin center.
Import the call center definition in Salesforce with its CTI Adapter URL set to the widget URL.
Upload the call center definition on the Data synchronization from external CRMs page in Copilot Service admin center.
Paste the customer-facing chat widget script into the call center definition in Salesforce.

questions.answer: Copy the widget URL from the Conversation widget tab in Copilot Service admin center, import the call center definition in Salesforce with its CTI Adapter URL set to the widget URL, and then add the user through Manage Call Center Users in Salesforce.
questions.explanation: The widget URL comes first because the call center definition needs it as its CTI Adapter URL. The call center must then exist in Salesforce before anyone can be added to it, so importing the definition comes before Manage Call Center Users. The definition belongs in Salesforce, because its Call Center setup is where the call center is created. The adapter URL points to the embedded widget for representatives, not to the customer-facing chat script.

optionExplanations.a: Correct as the third step. Manage Call Center Users adds users to a call center, so the imported call center has to exist first.
optionExplanations.b: Correct as the first step. The URL is listed under Integration into third-party systems on the Conversation widget tab, and the definition needs it.
optionExplanations.c: Correct as the second step. It needs the widget URL, and it creates the call center that users are added to.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. The definition is imported through Call Center in Salesforce Setup. The page named here syncs CRM data into Dataverse.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. The definition carries the embedded widget URL for representatives as its CTI Adapter URL. A customer-facing chat script doesn't belong there.

questions.prompt:
Tarn Valley Telecom wants to try the Telecom industry template in Service Operations Agent, which is a preview feature, before it decides whether to build an AI-first contact center. The voice channel is provisioned, and consumption-based billing is set up. The number the team will select is on the Trial Support voice workstream.

You need to plan the template run.

What should you choose for each item?

rows.label: What the setup does with the selected number

options.text: Keeps it on Trial Support and shares it with a new workstream
Moves it from Trial Support to a new workstream
Keeps Trial Support as is and acquires a new number for the setup

rows.label: Roles for the person who runs the setup

options.text: Omnichannel administrator and Omnichannel supervisor
System administrator and App Profile Manager Administrator
System administrator and Omnichannel administrator

rows.label: Response if the setup reports LatestPublishedVersionNotFound

options.text: Republish Transformation Agent Chat Bot in Copilot Studio
Delete and recreate the D365 Contact Center MCP Connection
Connect Application Insights to Dynamics 365 Contact Center

questions.answer: Selected number: Moves it from Trial Support to a new workstream. Roles: System administrator and Omnichannel administrator. LatestPublishedVersionNotFound: Republish Transformation Agent Chat Bot in Copilot Studio.
questions.explanation: The template doesn't leave the selected number where it is. It creates a new workstream, detaches the selected number from its existing workstream settings and attaches it to the new workstream, so anything that still routes through Trial Support loses that number. Service Operations Agent on its own needs the Omnichannel administrator role, but the industry template lists both System administrator and Omnichannel administrator as prerequisites. For the LatestPublishedVersionNotFound error, Microsoft directs you to Copilot Studio to republish Transformation Agent Chat Bot.

optionExplanations.r1a: Fails. The setup detaches the selected number from its existing workstream settings.
optionExplanations.r1b: Correct. The system creates a new workstream, detaches the selected number from the existing workstream settings and attaches it to the new workstream.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. The administrator selects a configured number in the setup, and that number is attached to the new workstream.
optionExplanations.r2a: Fails. The Omnichannel administrator role is enough to access Service Operations Agent, but the template's prerequisites also list System administrator.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. The template's prerequisites list Omnichannel administrator, and this pair doesn't include it.
optionExplanations.r2c: Correct. The template's prerequisites list both roles.
optionExplanations.r3a: Correct. Microsoft's note for this error says to go to Transformation Agent Chat Bot in Copilot Studio and republish the agent.
optionExplanations.r3b: Fails. Recreating this connection is the response when the agent can't perform actions or retrieve information, not the documented response to this error.
optionExplanations.r3c: Fails. Application Insights is a prerequisite for the agent to troubleshoot issues during setup. It isn't the documented response to this error.

questions.prompt:
Penhallow Legal Aid routes cases to representatives through unified routing and uses capacity profiles, not capacity units. Each representative must take:
- No more than three urgent cases a day
- No more than six standard cases a day
- No more than seven cases a day in total

The team will create three capacity profiles with End of day reset: Urgent with a limit of 3, Standard with a limit of 6, and Daily Total with a limit of 7. A case counts as urgent or standard according to its priority.

You need to configure routing so that every limit is enforced.

What should you choose for each item?

rows.label: Default profile on the workstream

options.text: Urgent
Standard
Daily Total

rows.label: Way to add the Urgent or Standard profile to a case

options.text: A rule output in a classification ruleset
A condition in the queue's assignment rules
A rule output in a route-to-queue ruleset

rows.label: Profiles assigned to each representative

options.text: Daily Total only
Urgent and Standard only
All three profiles

questions.answer: Workstream default: Daily Total. Adding the priority profile: A rule output in a classification ruleset. Representatives: All three profiles.
questions.explanation: Every case has to count against the overall limit, so Daily Total is the workstream's default profile. A classification ruleset then appends Urgent or Standard according to the case's priority. Each case now carries two profiles, and unified routing looks for a representative with available capacity in both. Capacity is consumed from both when the case is assigned. That's why representatives need all three profiles, and why no capacity-specific assignment rules are needed at queue level.

optionExplanations.r1a: Fails. Setting this on the workstream would apply it to every case, so standard cases would consume the urgent limit.
optionExplanations.r1b: Fails. Setting this on the workstream would apply it to every case, so urgent cases would consume the standard limit.
optionExplanations.r1c: Correct. The workstream's profile applies to every work item routed through it, which is what the overall limit needs.
optionExplanations.r2a: Correct. A classification ruleset can set a capacity profile as a rule output, and the profile is appended to the work item alongside the workstream's profile.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. Microsoft says that you needn't define assignment rules specific to capacity profiles at queue level, because the system matches the profile attached to the work item.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. Route-to-queue rules send work to a queue. The documented places to set a capacity profile are the workstream and a classification ruleset.
optionExplanations.r3a: Fails. A case also carries Urgent or Standard, and the assigned representative must have the matching profile.
optionExplanations.r3b: Fails. Every case carries Daily Total, so a representative without it wouldn't match.
optionExplanations.r3c: Correct. Each case carries Daily Total plus one other profile, and the documented design has representatives hold all three.

questions.prompt:
Sablewood Outfitters keeps Salesforce as its CRM. The connector for Salesforce syncs Contacts and Accounts into Dataverse, and it's active on the Data synchronization from external CRMs page in Copilot Service admin center. The data team is reviewing three items.

You need to decide how to handle each item.

What should you choose for each item?

rows.label: A representative finds an outdated phone number on a synced contact

options.text: Update the contact in Dataverse
Update the contact in Salesforce
Reset the connector's field mappings

rows.label: The security team asks to cut the connector's team to read access on the synced tables

options.text: Keep read and write, or synchronization fails
Accept it, because the connector reads only from Salesforce
Accept it, and reactivate the connector afterward

rows.label: Expected result after a mapped field is removed from the connector

options.text: Its existing values are deleted from Dataverse
Its existing values stay, and new data isn't synced
All field mappings return to the predefined defaults

questions.answer: Outdated phone number: Update the contact in Salesforce. Read-only request: Keep read and write, or synchronization fails. Removed field: Its existing values stay, and new data isn't synced.
questions.explanation: The connector brings data from Salesforce into Dataverse, and changes made to synced data in Dataverse aren't synced back, so corrections belong in Salesforce. The direction of the sync can suggest that the Dataverse side needs little access, but the selected team is what writes the data to Dataverse. It must have read and write permissions on the selected tables, or data synchronization fails. Removing a table or mapped field doesn't clean up what's there: the data remains in Dataverse, and only new data isn't synced.

optionExplanations.r1a: Fails. Microsoft recommends against changing synced data in Dataverse, because those changes aren't synced back to Salesforce.
optionExplanations.r1b: Correct. If synced data must change, Microsoft says to update it in Salesforce only.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. Reset returns the column mappings to the out-of-box mappings. It doesn't correct a value in a record.
optionExplanations.r2a: Correct. The team is used to write data to Dataverse, so it must have read and write permissions on the selected tables. Otherwise, data synchronization fails.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. Reading from Salesforce is only half of the sync. The connector's team writes to the Dataverse tables.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. The team must keep read and write permissions on the selected tables, and reactivating the connector doesn't remove that requirement.
optionExplanations.r3a: Fails. Microsoft says that the data remains in Dataverse when a table or mapped field is removed.
optionExplanations.r3b: Correct. The data remains in Dataverse, and only new data isn't synced.
optionExplanations.r3c: Fails. Returning to the defaults is what the Reset option does. Removing one field doesn't reset the other mappings.

questions.prompt:
Lakeshore Rail moved its production Dynamics 365 Contact Center environment to a new geography, and the organization is out of administration mode. Production uses voice on Azure Communication Services and record routing for email. The company then made a full copy of the moved environment to create a user acceptance testing (UAT) environment.

You need to complete the follow-up work.

What should you do for each item?

rows.label: Production: voice

options.text: Copy the new webhook endpoints into the Event Grid subscriptions
Disconnect the resource and connect a new one in the new geography
Turn off the voice channel and provision it again in Copilot Service admin center

rows.label: Production: record routing

options.text: Enable unified routing again
No extra steps
Configure and validate it separately

rows.label: UAT: real-time analytics reports

options.text: Import the msdyn_analytics records from production
Turn Enable Omnichannel real-time analytics off, then on
None, because the copied reports already read the UAT data

questions.answer: Production voice: Copy the new webhook endpoints into the Event Grid subscriptions. Production record routing: No extra steps. UAT real-time analytics reports: Turn Enable Omnichannel real-time analytics off, then on.
questions.explanation: The two operations leave different work. After a geo move, the contact center is recreated. The Azure Communication Services webhook endpoints change, so you copy the new values from Manage Azure Communication Services into the Event Grid subscriptions. Record routing needs no extra steps once the organization is out of administration mode. A copy is different: record routing would need separate configuration in the copy, and to make real-time reports reflect the target environment, you turn off Enable Omnichannel real-time analytics and turn it back on. Exporting msdyn_analytics isn't the way to do this, because that table holds organization-specific configuration.

optionExplanations.r1a: Correct. The webhook endpoints change for the new geography. The new values are in Copilot Service admin center, and you paste them into the corresponding Event Grid subscriptions.
optionExplanations.r1b: Fails. Connecting a target to its own resource is the guidance for an environment copy. After a geo move, you update the changed endpoints.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. Provisioning channels again is the follow-up for a reset, a restore or a tenant-to-tenant migration. It isn't among the post-move updates for a geo move.
optionExplanations.r2a: Fails. This is the follow-up for a reset, a restore or a tenant-to-tenant migration. The post-move updates say that no extra steps are needed.
optionExplanations.r2b: Correct. Record routing works after the organization is removed from administration mode.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. This is the guidance for an environment copy, where copying record-routing configuration isn't supported. It doesn't apply to the geo move.
optionExplanations.r3a: Fails. Microsoft recommends that you don't export the msdyn_analytics table, because it contains organization-specific configuration data.
optionExplanations.r3b: Correct. Microsoft says to turn this setting off and back on so that real-time reports reflect the target environment.
optionExplanations.r3c: Fails. The copy guidance says to turn the setting off and back on to make sure that the reports reflect the target environment.

questions.prompt:
Wexcombe Mutual releases its Dynamics 365 Contact Center configuration to production in managed solutions. During an incident, someone edited a session template directly in production. The next managed release imported successfully, but the template still shows the direct edit.

The release manager wants the direct edit gone, and wants the managed release to take effect. A colleague also proposes turning on the Block unmanaged customizations setting in production, which is off today, to stop further direct edits. Production receives Omnichannel upgrades, and Copilot Studio agents are published in it.

You need to choose how to handle each item.

What should you choose for each item?

rows.label: The direct edit on the session template

options.text: Edit the template directly in production so that it matches the release
Select Remove active customizations in the template's solution layers
Delete the managed solution from production, then import the release again

rows.label: The proposal to turn on Block unmanaged customizations

options.text: Reject it, because it also blocks removing unmanaged layers
Accept it, because Omnichannel upgrades are exempt from the setting
Reject it, because Omnichannel upgrades don't work with it on

questions.answer: Direct edit: Select Remove active customizations in the template's solution layers. Proposal: Reject it, because Omnichannel upgrades don't work with it on.
questions.explanation: An unmanaged customization sits on the top layer and defines runtime behavior, so a later managed release can import successfully without taking effect. Removing the active customization from the component's solution layers clears that layer and lets the managed value take effect. This can't be undone, so check the edit first. Editing the template again only adds to the unmanaged layer. The Block unmanaged customizations setting looks like the right control, but Microsoft lists Omnichannel install and upgrade, and publishing a Copilot Studio agent, among the known limitations. Microsoft recommends disabling the setting if you must use those features in the environment.

optionExplanations.r1a: Fails. Editing a managed configuration directly creates an active customization, so the unmanaged layer stays on the template.
optionExplanations.r1b: Correct. This command removes the unmanaged layer from a component that also has managed layers, and the managed release then defines the behavior.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. An active customization can make deleting the managed solution fail, and deleting a managed solution removes all of its components and related data.
optionExplanations.r2a: Fails. The conclusion is right, but this reason is wrong. Removing an unmanaged layer is one of the operations still allowed with the setting on.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. Omnichannel install and upgrade are on the known limitations list. Dataflows are the documented exception to the block, not Omnichannel.
optionExplanations.r2c: Correct. Omnichannel install and upgrade don't work with the setting on, and neither does publishing a Copilot Studio agent, so Microsoft recommends disabling it where those are needed.

questions.prompt:
Riverbend Credit Union is rolling out Copilot Service workspace and voice through Azure Communication Services to a new branch. The proposed desktop standard for representatives is:
- Browser: Google Chrome
- Browser policy: third-party cookies blocked in private browsing windows only
- Web filter: *.skype.com blocked, because the company has retired Skype
- Web filter: file-sharing category blocked, and no website on Microsoft's allow list is in that category
- Network: 6 Mbps upload and 10 Mbps download at each desk

Desktop notifications aren't needed. IT will change only the items that don't meet the stated requirements. An item that meets a minimum stays as it is.

You need to bring the standard in line with the system requirements for Dynamics 365 Contact Center.

Which two items should you change? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: The browser choice
The third-party cookie policy
The network bandwidth at each desk
The *.skype.com filter entry
The file-sharing category filter

questions.answer: The third-party cookie policy and the *.skype.com filter entry.
questions.explanation: Two items break a stated requirement. Dynamics 365 Contact Center uses third-party cookies for authentication, and Microsoft says to make sure they aren't blocked in any mode so that services such as presence work. If a URL filter is in use, the listed websites must be allowed as exceptions for users, and *.skype.com is on that list. The other three items meet the requirements. Google Chrome is a supported browser, 6 Mbps upload and 10 Mbps download are above the 4 and 8 Mbps minimums even though they're below the recommended 8 and 16 Mbps, and the category filter touches none of the listed websites.

optionExplanations.a: Fails. Google Chrome is listed as a supported browser. Microsoft Edge is named for the desktop notifications feature, which isn't needed here.
optionExplanations.b: Correct, and part of the solution. Third-party cookies are used for authentication and must not be blocked in any mode, or services such as presence might not work. Microsoft's advice to use normal mode doesn't change that.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. The bandwidth is below the recommended 8 Mbps upload and 16 Mbps download, but it's above the 4 and 8 Mbps minimums, and IT keeps items that meet a minimum.
optionExplanations.d: Correct, and part of the solution. This domain is on the list of websites to allow as exceptions when a URL filter is in use, whether or not the company uses Skype.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. A URL filter can block a category as long as the listed websites stay allowed, and none of them is in this category.

questions.prompt:
Fenwick Water routes email to representatives through record routing and uses capacity profiles. Representatives are reaching their limits because emails they've stopped working on still hold capacity. Some of those emails are finished, and others might need more work from someone else.

The team lead wants the capacity back today and accepts either outcome for an email: its work item closes, or it goes back to automatic assignment.

You need to release a representative's capacity from one of these emails.

Which two actions can you perform? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Deactivate the queue item that's assigned to the representative.
Close the email's session in Copilot Service workspace after the final reply.
Remove the representative's name from the Worked By field on the queue item.
Raise the representative's custom limit on the capacity profile that the email uses.
Set Assignment blocking to No on the capacity profile that the email uses.

questions.answer: Deactivate the queue item that's assigned to the representative, or remove the representative's name from the Worked By field on the queue item.
questions.explanation: Capacity release depends on the type of work. For conversations, capacity is released when the representative ends the conversation and closes the session. For cases, it's released when the case is resolved. Capacity isn't released automatically for activities such as email that are configured for record routing, so someone has to act on the queue item. The capacity page documents two actions. Deactivating the queue item closes the associated work item. Removing the representative from the Worked By field keeps the record open, and automatic assignment then tries to reassign the item. Changing a limit or a blocking setting doesn't release capacity that the email already holds.

optionExplanations.a: Correct, and a complete solution. Deactivating the queue item closes the associated work item, and the services that maintain capacity are updated.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. Closing the session is the release rule for conversations. Capacity isn't released automatically for activities such as email.
optionExplanations.c: Correct, and a complete solution. This is the documented option when the record needs to stay open, and automatic assignment then tries to reassign the item.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. A custom limit applies to new work assignments. It raises the ceiling, but the email still holds the capacity it consumed.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. Assignment blocking controls whether a representative gets new work items once the limit is met. It doesn't release what's already consumed.

questions.prompt:
Northgate Pharmacy wants ten simulated conversations against the inbound voice workstream for its Refills line. It will use agentic simulation in Dynamics 365 Contact Center, which is a preview feature. The voice channel is provisioned, the phone number is configured for simulation, representatives and routing are ready, and the journey has no keypad menu. Two test administrators in the same organization hold the required roles, and every prompt gives the workstream's phone number.

You need to choose a plan that the simulation can run.

Which two plans should you choose? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Submit one English prompt that requests ten conversations.
Have each administrator submit a five-conversation English prompt at the same moment.
Submit a five-conversation English prompt, and submit a second one after the first finishes.
Submit three English prompts one after another, requesting four, three and three conversations.
Submit a five-conversation English prompt, then a five-conversation Spanish prompt after it finishes.

questions.answer: Submit a five-conversation English prompt and a second one after the first finishes, or submit three English prompts one after another, requesting four, three and three conversations.
questions.explanation: Three limits shape the plan. A prompt can request up to five conversations, so ten conversations need at least two prompts. Only one simulation can be initiated and run at a time in one organization, so the prompts run in turn even with two administrators. Simulations are in English only. Any set of English prompts of five or fewer, run one after another, meets all three limits. The system also simulates at most two call conversations at once, so a run of five doesn't place all five calls together.

optionExplanations.a: Fails. A simulation prompt can request up to five conversations.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. Only one simulation can be initiated and run at a time in one organization, even when different administrators start them.
optionExplanations.c: Correct, and a complete solution. Each prompt stays within five conversations, the runs don't overlap, and both are in English.
optionExplanations.d: Correct, and a complete solution. Each prompt stays within five conversations and the runs don't overlap. Using more prompts than the minimum breaks no limit.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. Simulations are in the English language only, so the Spanish prompt can't run.

questions.prompt:
Cobble Hill Insurance has a production Dynamics 365 Contact Center environment with existing users and no associated security group. Administrators will associate a new Microsoft Entra security group with the environment. Five identities use the environment today, and none of them is in the group yet.

You need to identify the identities that must be added to the group before the association so that they keep working in the environment.

Which three identities should you add? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: A licensed representative
A user who holds the Dynamics 365 administrator role
A user who holds the Power Platform Administrator role
A non-interactive user account for a reporting connector
An application user for a server-to-server data integration

questions.answer: A licensed representative, a user who holds the Dynamics 365 administrator role, and a non-interactive user account for a reporting connector.
questions.explanation: Associating a security group with an existing environment disables the users who aren't members, so the question is which identities are exempt. Two are. A user with the Power Platform Administrator role shows as active and can sign in without being a member, and application users can run in any environment that's secured with a security group. The Dynamics 365 administrator role isn't exempt, because that user must be in the group to be enabled. Non-interactive users are also not exempt. Marking a user as non-interactive removes the license-specific provisioning rules, but security group rules still apply.

optionExplanations.a: Correct, and part of the solution. Associating the group disables users in the environment who aren't members.
optionExplanations.b: Correct, and part of the solution. A user with this role must be part of the security group before they're enabled in the environment.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. A user with this role who isn't in the group still shows as an active user and can sign in.
optionExplanations.d: Correct, and part of the solution. License-specific provisioning rules don't apply to these users, but security group rules still do.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. Application users can run in any environment that's secured with a security group, without being a member.

questions.prompt:
Thornbury Hotels configures its own Dynamics 365 Contact Center channels. Mina holds the Omnichannel administrator role. When she opens the WhatsApp account and Azure Communication Services settings, the secret values are hidden and she can't update them. Company policy doesn't allow her to hold the System Administrator role.

You need to give Mina access to those values.

What should you do?

options.text: Set Organization-level Read and Write on those tables in a custom role for her.
Add her current security role to the admin persona in Role persona mapping.
Grant read, update and create on those columns through a column security profile.
Assign the App Profile Manager Administrator role in addition to her current role.

questions.answer: Grant read, update and create on those columns through a column security profile.
questions.explanation: Administrators need column-level permissions on secure columns to configure features such as Azure Communication Services and the WhatsApp channel. Table privileges in a security role manage access at the table level, and a secured column has a separate control. Only users with the System Administrator role can reach a secured column unless a column security profile grants access. Microsoft's steps are to create or update a column security profile and give it read, update or create permissions on the columns that hold the secret attributes. The System Administrator role would bypass this, but policy rules it out.

optionExplanations.a: Fails. Security role privileges manage access at the table level. Users who aren't defined in a column security profile don't have access to a secured column.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. Persona mapping defines user permissions for unified routing by archetype. Column access for secrets comes from a column security profile.
optionExplanations.c: Correct. Microsoft's steps for secret attributes are to create or update a column security profile and give it permissions on those columns.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. This role's documented privileges cover profiles, templates and channel providers. Column permissions on secrets come from a column security profile.

questions.prompt:
Cedar Point Credit Union hires seasonal staff for chat. An administrator copies the Omnichannel agent role to a custom role named Seasonal Rep and assigns it to 30 licensed users. No other configuration has changed. In Enhanced user management, the users appear under All users but not under Contact center users, where the administrator wants to update their queues in bulk.

You need to make the 30 users appear under Contact center users.

What should you do?

options.text: Create a bookable resource record for each of the 30 users.
Add the Seasonal Rep role to the agent persona in Role persona mapping.
Set a default presence on the Omnichannel tab of each of the 30 users.
Add the Seasonal Rep role to a custom experience profile for Copilot Service workspace.

questions.answer: Add the Seasonal Rep role to the agent persona in Role persona mapping.
questions.explanation: The Contact center users view lists users who are assigned the representative, supervisor or admin persona, while All users lists all the Customer Service users. A persona comes from a role that's mapped to it. Dynamics 365 Contact Center maps its three primary roles by default, but a custom role has to be added to a persona. A copied role is a new role, and Microsoft's seasonal example selects it on the agent persona as a separate step. The other options are real settings that serve routing or the workspace experience, but they don't assign a persona.

optionExplanations.a: Fails. A bookable resource is what lets a user be assigned work through unified routing. The view is defined by persona, not by bookable resource.
optionExplanations.b: Correct. The view lists users who are assigned a persona, and this mapping gives holders of the custom role the agent persona.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. Default presence sets the status a representative is logged in with. It doesn't assign a persona.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Set rank and roles ties a security role to an experience profile, which targets the app experience. It doesn't assign the persona that this view is based on.

evidence.claim: When a queue item is deactivated, the associated live work item is closed, and the services that maintain presence and capacity are updated. For tables other than incident, Microsoft points to deactivating the queue item to release capacity.
evidence.applicability: Page dated 2026-08-25. This page also says that closing the underlying record deletes the queue item, and that changing the queue releases capacity. So the question offers no option about completing the email or moving it to another queue, because those are routes this question doesn't test. This page's closing guidance says tables other than incident need the queue item deactivated to release capacity, which agrees with the capacity page. The email routing page also says to make sure capacity is released after work on an email and points to the same section.

evidence.section: Note the following information about security groups; Review admin roles you need to complete different tasks
evidence.claim: When you associate a security group with an existing environment that has users, you disable all users in the environment who aren't members. A user with the Power Platform Administrator role who isn't in the group shows as active and can sign in. A Dynamics 365 administrator must be part of the group before being enabled. Application users can run in any environment secured with a security group without being a member.

evidence.section: Configure permissions to access secure columns
evidence.claim: Administrator users need column-level permissions on secure columns when they configure features including Azure Communication Services and the WhatsApp channel. In Power Platform admin center you create or update the column security profile and provide read, update or create permissions on the columns for the secret attributes.

evidence.section: Introduction; Add teams or users to a column security profile to control access
evidence.claim: Security role privileges manage access at the table level, and column-level security manages access to specific columns. Column-level security doesn't apply to users with the System Administrator role. Unless a security profile is assigned, only System Administrators can access a secured column, and users not defined in a profile don't have access.
